Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the quick intro yesterday. We’re moving forward with an initial pilot that needs dedicated GPU capacity across EU and APAC. High-level context:
- Workload: mixed chat + batch embedding jobs (search/semantic). Peak token throughput expected ~120k tokens/minute during daytime windows, steady baseline ~15k tokens/minute.
- Latency target: 95p < 300ms for chat inference in EU; APAC can tolerate slightly higher (~400ms).
- Data residency: EU customer PII must remain in-region. APAC workload is from Singapore/Japan.
- Timeline: pilot kickoff in early July, production by end of August if turnup goes well.

Asks: can Redwood provide a recommended pool topology (instance types, shard counts) and a suggested autoscale/burst policy that keeps cost predictable but covers daily traffic spikes? Also please send any SOW template or mutual action plan so procurement can start.

Attachments: high-level usage spreadsheet (attached) — filename: capacity_questionnaire.pdf

Appreciate a brief outline of next steps and an ops contact for the handoff.

Thanks Priya — summary and recommendations below (high level). I’ll put a slide with numbers after but wanted to get the proposal in front of Crestline so they can review ahead of the call.

Workload assumptions (validated from questionnaire): baseline token rate ~15k/min, predictable diurnal spikes to ~120k/min, batch embedding windows overnight (lower latency requirement).

Topology recommendations:
- EU primary cluster: 8 x A100-80GB (sharded across 2 pods of 4 GPUs). Reserve a minimum of 4 GPUs for steady-state (baseline), autoscale up to 8 for normal peaks.
- APAC cluster: 4 x A100-80GB (single pod), reserve 2 GPUs baseline, autoscale to 4 for peak windows.
- Model variants: run a quantized 8-bit variant for batch embeddings (cost savings), full precision for chat latency-critical routes.

Autoscale / burst policy (initial):
- Autoscale trigger: CPU/GPU utilization >= 70% sustained for 30s AND token queue length > 2000 tokens.
- Rapid-burst buffer: allow temporary burst capacity of +50% (i.e., additional ephemeral GPUs) for up to 10 minutes during scheduled peak windows (morning business hours). Ephemeral capacity billed at a higher rate — include in SOW as "burst hours" line item.
- Fallback: if regional capacity constrained, route non-PII chat traffic to the nearest compatible region (APAC <-> EU only for non-PII). PII strictly pinned to EU.

Operational notes:
- KV/prefix caching recommended for chat to reduce per-token compute on warm sessions.
- Warm-up plan: pre-warm 2 GPUs in EU 15 minutes before expected morning peak.
- Monitoring: per-route latency SLOs and token-level billing enabled; send alerts if cost delta > 15% monthly forecast.

Attachments: pool-topology-proposal.pdf (includes costs, shard diagrams, and simulated latency curves)

Happy to walk through these on the call.

Karthik Iyer
Capacity & Serving Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: EU + APAC initial ask — implementation considerations

Thanks Karthik — this looks reasonable. A few implementation notes from CS/Implementation side:

- Region selection: EU cluster should be in eu-west-1 to satisfy data residency and connectivity to their EU customers. APAC in ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo) for lower latency to Japan and Singapore (they can use edge peering).
- Routing policy: recommend active/passive for EU (active), active/standby for APAC with automated failover to EU for non-PII only.
- Autoscale and billing cadence: we should include a monthly burst-hour cap in the SOW (suggest 200 burst-hours for the initial quarter) with an overage rate. This prevents surprise charges while giving Crestline breathing room.
- Ops handoff items: runbook, maintenance windows (weekends preferred), SLA exceptions, and an onboarding runbook session (60–90 minutes) with their SREs during the first week.

I’ll coordinate with Marissa to capture milestones (kickoff, staging turnup, production cutover, post-launch review).

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success — Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
